Owner proposal of 2026-10-28 (task unit pool with inbox, execution and completed folders and a result Yaml per unit), the owner refinement that each execution runs at most 15 minutes before yielding so other tasks can be scheduled, and the owner approval to draft the design plus the queue skeleton for review. The design doc grounds the problem in the 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-28 run records (37 to 50 minute segment runs, the 0230 segment 2 stand-down against a concurrent Zombie Invasion session, the 1843 expiry crunch, the 18 run outcome_unknown lock) and specifies the unit schema, priorities by expiry, atomic rename claiming, 20 minute leases with a reaper, a single device token so contention queues instead of colliding, the 15 minute batch cap with partial release, and a three step migration (shadow mode, segment 2 pilot, full switch on the owner word). The _queue_ type is registered in typed-folder-adoption in this same commit per the registry rule. tools/queue.py implements enqueue, list, next, claim, complete, release, token acquire and release, and reap with only file operations, and was self-tested end to end in a scratch root (priority pick by expiry, token mutual exclusion, claim and complete with result block, expired lease reaped back to inbox). Nothing in the live routine changed - the segment crons keep running until the owner approves the migration. No game input was dispatched in this action.

Owner refinement of 2026-10-28 to the task unit queue draft - each task unit shall carry structured Yaml describing the task, where it is, and its result stats, so tools can gather stats and status and make reports reliably. The unit format is now one structured YAML frontmatter per unit (task fields, claim fields, and a result mapping with fixed core fields plus an open per-activity stats mapping); the fenced body block from draft 0.1.0 is removed so no report ever scrapes prose. tools/queue.py was rewritten on a small built-in YAML subset parser and serializer (no external dependency), complete now writes the result section into the frontmatter with duration and claimed count and repeatable --stat key=value entries, and a new stats subcommand aggregates counts by state and regular, result status totals, durations, late finishes, expired waiting units and overdue claims in text, YAML or JSON. Self-tested end to end in a scratch root, including a first-test failure (claim into a not yet created claimed folder) that was fixed by creating state folders on demand and retested green. The design doc moved to version 0.2.0 with sections 4, 5 and 7 updated. Live routine unchanged, still under owner review.

Owner direction of 2026-10-28 refining the task unit queue draft - the 15 minute cap is per unit (not per batch), the main agent's job becomes an executor loop that keeps executing tasks where needed, and a long activity such as Zombie Invasion keeps executing as a chain of units until its stop condition (zombies cleared) while other tasks ingest at unit boundaries when their time arrives. Design doc to version 0.3.0 - executor loop replaces the batch concept in sections 2 and 6, continuation chains and background priority 4 added, chain_id, chain_seq, attempts and max_attempts added to the unit schema, open questions 2 and 3 recorded as resolved by the owner, and one honest limit noted (the loop runs inside agent sessions and scheduled triggers, not as a literal daemon). tools/queue.py enforces the cap at enqueue (est_minutes above 15 refused), auto-numbers chain units, increments attempts on claim, and dead-letters a unit to done with status failed when attempts are exhausted on release or reap; stats gains per-chain done and pending counts. Self-tested in a scratch root - over-cap refusal, chain numbering, priority and expiry pick ahead of background units, and the third release dead-lettering the unit as failed. Live routine unchanged, still under owner review.

Owner direction of 2026-10-28 simplifying the scheduling mechanism - the 3 segment schedules are retired in the design; a single regular ticker task (for example every 30 minutes) checks whether any tasks need to be executed, puts them into execution, and skips silently when there are none. Design doc to version 0.4.0 - section 6 now specifies the ticker (reap, produce idempotently from the tracker, execute the loop within a proposed 25 minute pass budget, silent skip), the device token as the overlap guard between ticks, bounded latency (one interval plus the remainder of the running unit, itself capped at 15 minutes), earliest-expiry picking, and the stats late list as the feedback signal for shortening the interval. Section 7 records that the segment field survives only as a reporting tag, and section 8 migration becomes shadow mode with the execute step disabled, then a single switch that deletes the segment crons and folds the Zombie Invasion rounds cron into chain production, then a settle period tuning only the interval and the pass budget. tools/queue.py needed no change - the ticker is composed entirely of its existing primitives (reap, enqueue, next, claim, complete, token, stats) plus the tracker due list. Live segment crons unchanged, still under owner review.

Owner directions of 2026-10-28 - implement the queue after validation and move the entire execution to it; one task unit per task type so statistics show execution quality per type; typical execution time per type learned as data accumulates; each unit records start and end time with its status and stats (already the result schema - started_at from the claim stamp, finished_at and duration_seconds stamped by the complete command). Implementation - regulars.py gained a --json due list; queue.py gained sync (reap plus idempotent production from the tracker, VIP expiry stamped from the next 19:00 local reset, learned est_minutes), chain homogeneity enforcement (a chain refuses a second task type), per-type quality statistics (done, failed, late, duration average and max, learned typical minutes with sample count), and typical_minutes (median of completed durations, static defaults until 3 samples). Validation in scratch roots covered sync idempotency, reaping inside sync, the chain type refusal, and learned estimates (600, 660, 720 second samples yield an 11 minute estimate); a live shadow sync matched the tracker due set exactly (empty at that moment). Cutover - the four old schedule definitions were backed up to the goal backup folder under cutover-2026-10-28, the ticker lastwar-queue-ticker (every 30 minutes, full authorization, red lines, recording and reporting rules) was created, the three segment schedules and the Zombie Invasion rounds schedule were deleted, the goal GOAL.md routine structure was rewritten, and a first manual ticker run was queued for end-to-end validation. The design doc is now version 0.5.0 with status implemented. The Slack round summary schedule is unchanged and keeps reading _records_, which ticker passes keep writing per unit.

Owner directions of 2026-10-28 - a system shall regularly add tasks to the pool: check every four hours and add task units for the next 12 hours of work, with no duplication, where duplication means the exact same task unit for the same time slot added again when it is already there; the four hour tasks recur at every four hour boundary. Implementation - units gained planned_for (the cadence window they serve) and not_before; the (regular, planned_for) pair is the anti-duplication invariant enforced in one shared production path used by both the planner and the ticker sync, checked across inbox, claimed and done. queue.py gained a plan command projecting every regular's windows (every-run at the 4 hour anchors, daily-reset at the 19:00 reset, weekly-thu on Thursdays) over a 12 hour horizon, consulting the tracker so a regular already done for the current slot gets no phantom unit; pick and claim refuse units before their not_before; reap now also expires inbox units whose window fully passed into done with status expired. Validated in scratch (65 staged over 12 hours including the current slot; second plan added 0; sync added 0 against the planner's pool; future claims refused; duel window text stamped, for example duel day 3 radar release), then run live - 48 future units staged for the slots starting 06:03, 06:30 and 06:57 through the 14:xx slots, 17 current-slot items skipped as already done, and next correctly returned nothing while all 48 are upcoming. The planner schedule lastwar-queue-planner (every 4 hours) was created; the device token file is now gitignored as transient state. Design doc to version 0.6.0 with the planner as section 7.
